findings.issue_key: uncategorized pill count includes title check
findings.element: Uncategorized pill '{count} need(s) a category or title' (mobile) / banner (md+)
findings.experience: The pile count includes rows that already have a category but whose bank descriptor looks cryptic (e.g. 'STARBUCKS #4412'). The user sees '12 need a category or title' when 2 need a category, opens Review, and is walked through already-categorized rows asking for a title. 'All caught up' is unreachable without retitling every row.
findings.why: page.tsx:201 adds a row to attentionIds when `isUncat || looksCryptic(t.description)`; title.ts:141 flags any all-caps string containing a digit. The product model says a title must never be required and the only daily job is categorizing.
findings.change: page.tsx:204: build the pill/queue from `uncategorizedIds` only (drop `looksCryptic` from the queue). Change the pill copy at uncategorized-review.tsx:62 to '{count} uncategorized'. Keep the Title field on the card but collapse it behind a 'Rename' link so it is visibly optional. If retitling is wanted, surface it as a separate low-key count elsewhere, never in the pile.

code_refs.note: pill copy 'need a category or title'

screens: /transactions (inline panel under a saved row after tapping 'Splits')
findings.experience: The natural GST order is: Add split, type 2.50 into the new row, then hit the shortcut to fix the first row. Because the new row is now the last row and the remaining is -2.50, the shortcut subtracts 2.50 from the row the user just typed, resetting it to 0.00. The user sees their GST amount vanish and the chip still unbalanced.
findings.why: The shortcut always mutates copy[copy.length - 1] (split-editor.tsx:169-170). After 'Add split' (split-editor.tsx:154 appends) the last row is the freshly typed GST row, so the helper the comment at split-editor.tsx:19-21 promises ('without running mental arithmetic') only works if the user first edits the original row by hand, which is exactly the arithmetic it was meant to remove.
findings.change: Apply the remainder to the row that was NOT most recently edited: track lastEditedKey in updateRow and target the first row whose key !== lastEditedKey (fallback: row 0). Relabel the button 'Put $x on <category or 'row 1'>'. Additionally render a per-row 'Fill remaining' text button (min-h 44px) inside each amount cell when that row is not the one just edited.

code_refs.note: Add split appends, so the new GST row becomes 'last'

findings.element: StatTile 'Net' (compact, mobile) and its md+ twin
findings.experience: Net = outflow - inflow, so spending $3,000 against $1,000 income shows 'Net $2K' in green with no sign, while a month where income exceeds spending shows red. The user cannot tell whether the number is money left over or money spent, and the colour says the opposite of what they expect.
findings.why: page.tsx:154 `net = outflow - inflow`; page.tsx:279-280 `tone={net >= 0 ? 'leaf' : 'maple'}`; Amount is rendered with compact and no sign (amount.tsx:29-30 ignores `sign` when compact). Rows use '-' for outflow, so the tile's unsigned positive contradicts the list.
findings.change: Either flip to `net = inflow - outflow`, label it 'Left over', tone leaf when >= 0 / maple when < 0, and render `<Amount sign='always'>` (add sign support to the compact branch in amount.tsx:29); or keep the maths, label it 'Net spent', and tone maple when > 0. Also add a one-word caption when a filter is active (e.g. 'filtered') so the tiles are not mistaken for the month total.

findings.issue_key: U03:19 need a category or title review pill
findings.element: '19 need a category or title · Review' pill -> Categorize transactions dialog
findings.experience: Tapping the butter-colored pill at the very top of the transactions page opens a modal that steps through uncategorized transactions one at a time (progress '1 of 19', Save & next / Skip, a progress bar whose accessible name is literally 'Triage progress').
findings.why: The product model states the user never wants a separate review/triage step and that categorizing in place is the whole job. The component's own doc-comment calls itself 'a focused triage queue' - this is a purpose-built review-mode UI, prominently placed as the first thing under the month picker, competing with the in-place 'Categorize' button that already exists on every uncategorized row (and which is the correct pattern - see J1b-F5).
findings.change: Retire the modal triage flow (uncategorized-review.tsx) or demote it to an optional, out-of-the-way affordance; keep the count as a passive badge if useful, but stop routing the primary CTA into a one-at-a-time review dialog. Rely on the inline 'Categorize' button already on each row in the normal list, which already matches the model.

findings.issue_key: U04:balanced remaining badge and the apply x
findings.element: 'Balanced'/'Remaining' badge and the 'Apply $X to last split' shortcut inside the split editor
findings.experience: Right after typing the GST split's amount (25.00) with the original Transportation split still at 500.00, the badge kept showing '✓ Balanced' even though the two rows summed to $525 against a $500 total. After I corrected the Transportation row to 475.00, the badge flipped the other way to 'Remaining -$25.00' and offered 'Apply -$25.00 to last split' - both wrong, since 475+25 already equalled the $500 total. The badge is a beat behind whatever you just typed.
findings.why: MoneyInput's onChange only updates local text state (setRaw); the onCents callback that feeds the parent's `rows` state - and therefore `currentSum`/`remaining`/`balanced` - fires only on blur. The split editor's live balance feedback is computed from state that lags one field-blur behind what's on screen, so exactly the arithmetic-checking task this feature exists for (see whether your split adds up) gives false answers mid-edit.
findings.change: Fire onCents on every valid keystroke (debounced) in MoneyInput, not only onBlur, so `currentSum`/`remaining`/`balanced` in split-editor.tsx track the visible input text live. At minimum, recompute balance on input, not just blur.

code_refs.note: onCents (feeds parent balance calc) fires only onBlur
currentSum/remaining derived from rows state that onCents feeds
'Apply {remaining} to last split' button uses the same stale remaining

findings.issue_key: U04:both split rows category dropdowns in th
screens: /transactions - inline Split editor, immediately after Save splits
findings.element: Both split rows' category dropdowns in the still-open editor
findings.experience: After a successful Save splits, both category selects in the editor snap to '- Uncategorized -' while the amounts (475.00/25.00) stay correct. The row summary directly above (still on screen) correctly reads 'Split: Transportation + Audit GST', and the categorization is genuinely saved (confirmed on /budgets and by closing/reopening the same editor). But the form you're looking at right after the save you just made tells you your categorization is gone.
findings.why: The split editor's local `rows` state isn't re-synced from the server's fresh, correctly-saved data after the Server Action + revalidatePath completes, so the open form momentarily shows a state that doesn't match reality. This is the same class of bug flagged in J2 (category add stuck for 6+ minutes on stale client state despite a 200 server response) and J3 (4 of 6 inline categorize actions visually reverted to Uncategorized despite succeeding server-side) - a recurring pattern where a successful mutation's own screen doesn't reflect the truth without a manual reload or re-open.
findings.change: After a successful saveSplits, re-initialize the editor's `rows` state from the action's returned/re-fetched split data (or close the editor automatically on success, since the row summary above already shows the result) instead of leaving stale local state rendered over a form whose categories now silently don't match what got saved.

code_refs.note: rows state initialized once from initialSplits; never re-synced after a successful save
success branch only shows a 'Splits saved.' message; does not reconcile rows

findings.issue_key: U03:fixed install maple hint card position f
findings.element: Fixed 'Install Maple' hint card (position: fixed, z-20) above the mobile tab bar
findings.experience: The install-hint banner does not scroll with the page. As I scrolled the transaction list, it sat squarely on top of whatever row was at that vertical band - once directly over the Aug 24 Uber row, and again directly over the quick-category chip picker's Audit GST / Miscellaneous / More / +New buttons when I opened Categorize on the Gusto payroll deposit. The tool's own click-safety check independently confirmed the same thing on the dashboard: an account card tap was rejected because the click point was 'covered by <div.maple-chrome.fixed>'.
findings.why: The core daily job of this app is tapping a transaction row to categorize or split it in place. A persistent floating card that can land on top of the exact controls you need to tap - with no guarantee of where in the scroll it ends up - is direct friction on that one task, and it can silently eat taps (the user thinks they tapped 'Miscellaneous' and instead tapped the install card).
findings.change: Stop reserving space only at the bottom of the page (--maple-hint-h padding helps only the very last row). Either: (a) give the hint's outer wrapper pointer-events:none and only the inner white card pointer-events:auto so taps that land on its transparent margin fall through, (b) auto-hide the hint whenever a row's action panel (Categorize / Splits / Edit) is expanded, or (c) replace the persistent fixed card with a one-time auto-dismissing toast that never sits mid-list for more than a few seconds.

code_refs.note: fixed inset-x-0 z-20 wrapper, bottom: calc(72px + safe-area) - floats over mid-scroll content, not just the list's end
height is published only to pad the page's bottom, which does nothing for rows the fixed card passes over while scrolling

findings.element: Accounts empty state 'Add one' and spending empty state 'Add some'
findings.experience: New user with a linked bank but nothing categorised reads 'No categorised expenses this month. Add some.' and taps into a manual add form. With no accounts they read 'No accounts yet. Add one' and land on the accounts list rather than the bank link.
findings.why: Both empty states word the next step as adding (client.tsx:458-461, :595-598) even though the model says transactions arrive by themselves and the job is to categorise them; the accounts link goes to /accounts instead of the Plaid connect flow.
findings.change: Accounts empty: 'No accounts yet.' + Button 'Link a bank' -> /transactions/import/plaid-setup and a text link 'or add a cash account' -> /accounts. Spending empty: 'Nothing categorised yet this month.' + link 'Categorise what came in ->' to /transactions?uncategorized=1 (0 uncategorized: 'No spending recorded this month.').

code_refs.note: accounts empty state links to /accounts 'Add one'

findings.experience: Every incoming row needs a tap on 'Categorize' just to reveal the chips, then a second tap to pick. With 15 new rows that is 30 taps and 15 panel open/close animations for a job the model says should be one gesture per row.
findings.why: row.tsx:251-264 toggles `categorizing`; the chips only mount at row.tsx:320-329. The product model calls per-row hunting/extra steps friction.
findings.change: For rows where `isUncategorized && canEdit`, render the top-6 chip strip (horizontally scrollable, `hide-scroll`) directly under the meta line instead of the 'Categorize' button; keep 'More...' and '+ New' as the last two chips. Drop the toggle. The 'Uncategorized' badge stays as the label for the strip.

findings.experience: For a category outside the top 6 the path is Categorize -> More... -> open picker -> scroll wheel -> Done -> Apply: 5-6 taps. The extra 'Apply' after the native picker already committed a value is pure overhead.
findings.why: quick-categorize.tsx:108-123 stores the select value and requires a separate Apply button.
findings.change: Call apply(v) directly from CategorySelect onChange (ignore ''); remove the Apply button. Same in the triage card: selecting from the select at uncategorized-review.tsx:361-366 should also be the only step needed if the user then taps Save.

findings.experience: The household owner opens the app to a green net-worth hero and a month greeting. Nothing on the screen says '7 transactions came in and need a category' or offers a one-tap way to the pile. The only primary action on the screen is the manual '+' add.
findings.why: The product model says the whole daily job is categorizing what arrived; page.tsx never queries uncategorized rows and WIDGETS has no such card (client.tsx:35-48), so the cold-open screen cannot show the one thing the user came for (J3).
findings.change: In page.tsx add a query for current-month transactions whose single split has category_id null (same rule as transactions/page.tsx:190-200) returning count + sum. Add a 'needs-categorizing' widget to WIDGETS and to DEFAULT_LAYOUT immediately after 'greeting'. It renders nothing when count is 0; otherwise a single tappable Card: '7 to categorize · $412.30' with a leaf 'Categorize ->' link to /transactions?uncategorized=1 (add that param handler on the transactions page so it scrolls to / expands the uncategorized list).

code_refs.note: transactions query selects only amount/member/account; no split/category state

findings.experience: Rows dated the 29th-31st that Plaid delivered on the 1st are not in the pile when the user opens Transactions (defaults to this month). The pill says nothing about them; the user has to know to tap '<' and look. With a search or account filter active the count silently drops to the filtered subset.
findings.why: The transactions query is bounded to [month, nextMonth) (page.tsx:90-91) and attentionIds is built from the already-filtered `transactions` array (page.tsx:196). The product model says the user must never hunt for the pile.
findings.change: Add a second lightweight query in page.tsx (transaction_splits where category_id is null joined to editable transactions, no month bound) and pass `totalUncategorized` + `olderUncategorized` to UncategorizedReview. Pill copy: '5 uncategorized · 2 from July'. Tapping the pill opens the queue over ALL uncategorized rows (ordered newest first), not the month slice. Ignore search/account/scope filters for the count.

screens: /categories (shell parent /setup, top-left back chevron; only in-app link is the Budgets empty state)
findings.experience: The sheet draws an iOS grab handle at the top, so the user swipes down to close it. Nothing happens; they must reach the X in the top-right corner.
findings.why: The handle is a decorative div (sheet.tsx:113) with no touch handlers; the only dismissals are the top-right X, the scrim, and Esc.
findings.change: Add pointer handlers on the panel header/handle: track vertical drag, translate the panel with the finger, and call onClose when released past 80px or with downward velocity; snap back otherwise. Keep the X.

code_refs.note: only explicit close is the top-right X
scrim click is the only touch dismiss

findings.experience: The save confirmation renders as a plain aria-live='polite' paragraph inside the form (12.5px text), not the app's usual role='status' toast used elsewhere (e.g., Delete, rule creation). My toast watcher, which listens for role='status' the way the rest of the app signals success, caught nothing at all. Since Save splits sits ~350-400px below where you tapped Splits, a user who has scrolled at all by the time they tap Save could easily miss this text entirely.
findings.why: Inconsistent success-feedback mechanism versus the rest of the app makes 'did that work?' harder to answer for this specific, easy-to-miss location, and breaks automated/assistive tooling that watches for the app's standard toast pattern.
findings.change: Fire the same toast/role='status' component used elsewhere in the app on a successful split save, in addition to (or instead of) the inline paragraph.

code_refs.note:
success message rendered as inline

, not the app's toast system

findings.experience: Opened Splits on an uncategorized $100 withdrawal, entered two rows (Transportation $70 / Personal $30), then tapped 'Hide splits' (the closest thing this inline editor has to a dismiss). Reopening Splits on the same row shows a single default row again: the full $100, category reset to '- Uncategorized -'. The two-row draft is gone with no warning. A reload after refilling the same two rows confirmed the same total loss (row reverts to plain 'Uncategorized -$100.00', no split UI open at all).
findings.why: This editor is not a dialog - it has no scrim, no Close button, and Escape does nothing (confirmed: pressing Escape left both rows exactly as typed, because there's no listener to catch it). The only way to leave it is to collapse the row, and collapsing is exactly what happens on any real-world interruption (switching apps, a notification, a phone call) since `showSplits` is a plain boolean that unmounts the child component. The product's whole premise is quick in-place edits that survive being interrupted; this one specific editor is the one place that silently punishes it.
findings.change: Lift the split-row draft state (categories + amounts, not just the saved value) up to the parent `TransactionRow` (or a row-keyed cache) so it survives `showSplits` toggling to false and back to true, and clear it only on an explicit Save or an explicit 'discard' action - not on mere collapse.

code_refs.note: {showSplits && (<SplitEditor .../>)} - conditional mount/unmount discards all child state

findings.experience: The user thumbs down the page from the top; the thumb lands on the 150px chart band inside the hero and the page does not scroll, the scrub dot moves instead. They have to lift and re-drag from outside the chart.
findings.why: `touch-none` on the svg (client.tsx:334) disables browser panning over a 150px-tall, full-width area near the top of every cold open, in exchange for a scrub feature with no month axis to scrub against.
findings.change: Change the svg class to `touch-pan-y` so vertical drags scroll and horizontal drags scrub, and only setScrubIdx when `e.pointerType !== 'touch' || Math.abs(dx) > Math.abs(dy)`. Clear scrubIdx on pointerup/pointercancel as well as pointerleave.

findings.experience: At a real keyboard-open viewport (390x508, keyboard top at 508px, matching this app's own keyboard height elsewhere), Save splits sits at y=500-544 - entirely below the visible viewport, under the fixed tab bar. This is the third distinct primary action in this app (after Add account in J1 and Save budgets in J2) that a keyboard hides on a phone.
findings.why: No form in this app appears to reserve space for, or scroll to reveal, its primary submit button when the on-screen keyboard is open near the bottom of a scrolling page - a systemic gap rather than a one-off bug in this screen.
findings.change: Give the split editor's action row the same fix needed everywhere else this recurs: either pin Save splits in a footer bar that sits above the keyboard (padding-bottom: env(keyboard-inset-height) equivalent / visualViewport-aware positioning), or scroll the focused input's container so the submit button stays in view when a MoneyInput is focused.

findings.issue_key: U00:whole dashboard body net worth card inco
findings.element: Whole dashboard body (net worth card, Income/Spent/Saved tiles, account rail, 'Where it went')
findings.experience: Cold-opening the dashboard with 19 transactions sitting uncategorized gives zero signal that anything needs attention: no count, no banner, no CTA. Confirmed programmatically - the page's own text contains no occurrence of 'uncategorized', 'review', or 'needs category'.
findings.why: The brief's whole product model is that categorizing is 'the user's whole daily job' - but the one screen the user opens every day never says the job exists. A user has to already know to tap into Transactions to discover the pill.
findings.change: Add a dashboard tile/banner (near the top, above 'Where it went') reading e.g. '19 transactions need a category' that deep-links straight to the first uncategorized row on Transactions, and keep it in sync with the same count the Transactions pill shows.

code_refs.note: 'Uncategorized' only appears as a fallback label inside the spending-by-category breakdown, never as a count/CTA.

findings.issue_key: U00:quick category chip more full select app
findings.element: Quick category chip / 'More…' full-select Apply / '+ New' Create & apply (inline row actions)
findings.experience: In 4 of 6 in-place categorization attempts (McDonald's chip, Amazon full-select, Touchstone full-select, Sent '+ New'), the panel closed immediately after the tap and the row reverted to showing 'Uncategorized' with the Categorize button back - indistinguishable from the tap having failed. Network inspection showed every one of those POSTs actually returned 200, and the true category only appeared in the row after a full page reload.
findings.why: The core promise of this screen is 'tap a chip, see it categorized, move on.' When the client silently fails to reflect a successful save, a user has no way to tell success from failure without opening devtools - they'll very plausibly re-tap, second-guess the app, or give up on a row they actually already finished.
findings.change: Show the applied category optimistically the instant a chip/Apply/Create & apply is tapped (useOptimistic or local state update keyed off the response), and add a router.refresh()/cache-tag invalidation on the client after the server action resolves so the row never has to wait for an unrelated reload to catch up.

code_refs.note: apply() awaits setTransactionCategory then only calls onDone?.() to close the panel - no optimistic UI, no visible pending state, no client refresh.
setTransactionCategory does call revalidate() server-side - the DB write and revalidatePath calls are correct, so the gap is purely client-side reflecting the update.

screens: 'Always do this' rule sheet (opened from a row's 'Always share' button)
findings.experience: Tapped Create rule on a fully-filled-out Uber rule (merchant, category Transportation, Household-ratio share, apply-to-past checked). The button flipped to a disabled 'Saving…' and stayed there for 58+ seconds with no toast, no error, and no new network request ever visible. Only by navigating to /rules directly did I learn the rule had in fact been created and had already applied itself to 9 past transactions, retroactively marking 6 of them as household-shared.
findings.why: This is the exact 'set it once, stop re-categorizing this merchant forever' automation the product model exists to encourage, and its own save button hangs indefinitely with zero feedback - a real user would assume the app froze, likely force-closing the tab or re-submitting (risking duplicate rules) long before the change actually lands.
findings.change: Fix the client so the rule-creation mutation's resolution actually closes the dialog and shows a confirmation ('Rule created - 9 matches found, 6 now shared'); add a client-side timeout/error state so a genuinely stuck request tells the user something went wrong instead of hanging forever on a disabled button.

findings.issue_key: U00:need a category or title pill month navi
findings.element: 'need a category or title' pill / month navigator
findings.experience: The pill only counts the transactions in whichever month is currently in view. Paging back to July 2026 shows 18 transactions with 15 (83%) still Uncategorized - a backlog that's completely invisible from the August view, the pill, or the dashboard.
findings.why: If a user only ever glances at 'this month's' pill, a large and growing pile of older uncategorized transactions can sit forever with no signal it exists - directly undermining 'the user's whole daily job is to categorize them.'
findings.change: Make the pill (and any future dashboard banner) reflect a household-wide uncategorized count, not just the visible month, with a secondary line like '+15 more from earlier months' that jumps straight to the oldest unresolved month.

findings.issue_key: form server validates what client knows
screens: /transactions (inline panel under a saved row after tapping 'Splits')
findings.experience: The chip already says 'Remaining $2.50', but Save is enabled; the user taps it, waits for the server, then gets 'Splits must sum to the transaction total. Currently 55.00 vs 52.50.' at the bottom of the panel with no $ sign and, for income, negative numbers.
findings.why: Client knows `balanced` (split-editor.tsx:47) but only disables on hasInvalid. The server message uses toFixed(2) instead of formatMoney, so it does not match any other number on the screen.
findings.change: Disable Save when !balanced and set its label to 'Balance splits to save' (aria-disabled, keep it visible). Change actions.ts:354 to `Splits add up to ${formatMoney(sum)} but the transaction is ${formatMoney(txAmount)}.` using the same formatMoney as the header.

findings.experience: 'Save & next' is enabled with nothing chosen; tapping it advances, bumps the '{n} categorized' counter and ends on 'All caught up · Sorted 3 of 3' while the rows are still uncategorized. The progress readout lies.
findings.why: uncategorized-review.tsx:291-309 save() always calls onSaved(ids) regardless of categoryId; the button at :411-420 is disabled only while pending. Server side, category null is a valid write (actions.ts:269).
findings.change: Disable 'Save & next' unless `categoryId !== ''` or `description !== (txn.description ?? '')`; when only the title changed, do not add the id to savedCount ('categorized'). Rename the counter 'saved'.

screens: /transactions (inline panel under a saved row after tapping 'Splits')
findings.experience: Every GST split requires scrolling the native picker through the whole category tree to the same 'Tax/GST' entry; nothing remembers it and the new row starts as '- Uncategorized -' with no focus.
findings.why: SplitEditor is not given topCategoryIds (row.tsx:57 has it for QuickCategorize only) and has no recent-category memory; native select has no type-ahead on iOS.
findings.change: Pass topCategoryIds into SplitEditor and render up to 4 category chips (min-h 44px) above the select of a row whose category is null; default a new row's category to the most recent split category from localStorage('maple:lastSplitCategory').

findings.issue_key: U02:category spend totals dashboard where it
findings.element: Category spend totals (dashboard 'Where it went', budgets per-category 'Spent' figures)
findings.experience: 8 transactions this month sit Uncategorized (confirmed via /transactions' '8 need a category or title' pill). Confirmed in code that any split with no category_id is skipped when the dashboard builds its per-category spend map, so those 8 transactions - including an ambiguous merchant 'Fun -$89.40' that could plausibly be dining/food spend - are invisibly excluded from every 'Food' and 'Audit Food' number shown on both the dashboard and /budgets. Nothing on either page indicates that some of this month's spend hasn't been sorted yet.
findings.why: The whole product model is that transactions arrive and the user's job is to sort them into categories; while any are unsorted, every category total (including the one this journey needed - food) is silently incomplete, and the user has no way to know it from the dashboard or budgets screens.
findings.change: Surface the uncategorized count (or its dollar total) directly on the dashboard and on /budgets - e.g. a small 'N uncategorized ($X) not counted above' note near 'Where it went' and near the budgets hero, linking to the review flow.

code_refs.note: if (s.amount_cents <= 0 || !s.category_id) continue - uncategorized splits excluded from spendByCategory

findings.issue_key: U03:full category list 17 options offered wh
findings.element: Full category list (17 options) offered when categorizing an inflow
findings.experience: Categorizing a +$2,450.00 Payroll Deposit and a +$4.22 interest payment, I scanned the entire 'All categories' dropdown (Housing, Transportation, Food, Health, Personal, Subscriptions, Entertainment, Savings contribution, Taxes, Debt payment, Miscellaneous, plus household-created ones) - there is no Income, Salary, or Interest category anywhere, on an inflow-carrying account. I had to file both under 'Miscellaneous', the same bucket as ambiguous junk-drawer spend like 'Fun -$89.40'.
findings.why: The product model's daily job is accurate in-place categorization; when the category taxonomy has no slot for real income, every income figure on the dashboard's 'Where it went'/spend totals is silently contaminated by whatever else lands in Miscellaneous, and the user is forced into a categorization they know is wrong.
findings.change: Seed a default top-level 'Income' category (with common children like Salary, Interest, Transfers in) alongside the existing expense-oriented defaults, and have the quick-category chip ranking prefer it for transactions with a positive amount.

findings.issue_key: U02:dashboard for a household with zero acco
findings.element: Dashboard for a household with zero accounts (net-worth hero + Accounts empty state)
findings.experience: The first thing I see is a dark $0.00 Net worth card with a flat line and 1M/3M/YTD/1Y/ALL buttons, three $0.00 tiles, and then below the fold 'No accounts yet. Add one.' findings.issue_key: U00:sync now button per bank row
findings.experience: Tapping Sync now on a bank whose pill reads 'Re-auth needed' - with that exact bank visibly listed one line above the button - pops the alert 'No connected banks to sync.' findings.why: triggerPlaidSync's own item query filters `.in('status', ['active', 'error'])`, which deliberately excludes login_required items. findings.issue_key: plaid reauth status filter excludes target
findings.element: usePlaidReauth onSuccess -> triggerPlaidSync(id) -> actions.ts status filter
findings.experience: User taps 'Re-authenticate' on a bank stuck in login_required, completes Plaid Link update-mode successfully, sees 'Re-authenticated. Syncing…', but the bank still shows 'Re-auth needed' after refresh and never syncs again - re-auth appears to silently fail every time.
findings.why: triggerPlaidSync's item query filters .in('status', ['active','error']) even when a specific itemRowId is passed (actions.ts:426-431). Immediately after a successful update-mode Link, the plaid_items row is still status='login_required' (nothing sets it back to 'active' until a sync actually succeeds - see plaid-sync.ts:675-689 itemStatusFor). So the targeted post-reauth sync call finds zero matching rows, returns {error:'No connected banks to sync.'}, and that error is discarded by usePlaidReauth.onSuccess (plaid-connect.tsx:424-430), which unconditionally calls onDone() and reports success. The item is left permanently stuck in login_required with no automatic path out - the user must stumble on a bulk 'Sync all' or wait for the daily cron/webhook, neither of which is explained anywhere.
findings.change: In actions.ts triggerPlaidSync, when itemRowId is supplied (a direct, user-initiated resync of one item - especially right after reauth), do not apply the .in('status', ['active','error']) filter; only apply it to the bulk 'sync all' path (no itemRowId). This lets the targeted sync run regardless of the item's current status and actually clear login_required on success.

code_refs.note: itemRowId filter is ANDed with the status filter, not a replacement for it
triggerPlaidSync(id) result is awaited but never checked
onDone() fires unconditionally, reporting success regardless of sync outcome
status only flips to 'active' inside a successful syncPlaidItem run - which never gets a chance to run here

findings.experience: After accepting the 14-row mapping wizard's defaults and tapping 'Link & sync', the button read 'Saving...' with no spinner, no toast, and no other change on the page for roughly 40 seconds before the wizard finally collapsed into a linked/synced state.
findings.why: Same pattern as J2-F1 (category add hanging on 'Adding...'): the underlying mutation appears to commit quickly server-side, but the client-side pending UI drags on far longer than the actual work with zero indication of progress. A real user staring at a static 'Saving...' button for the better part of a minute - on the single highest-value action in this whole journey - would reasonably conclude the app froze, and either back out (losing the mapping work) or tap again (risking a duplicate bank link).
findings.change: Investigate the shared root cause with J2-F1 (React 19 Server Action / revalidation not resolving the pending state promptly for larger mutations). At minimum, add an incremental progress indicator ('Linking 14 accounts...', or per-account ticks) so 40+ seconds of silence doesn't read as a hang.

findings.issue_key: U05:account select category select and descr
findings.element: Account select, Category select, and Description input inside `AddTransactionForm`
findings.experience: Filled Amount=4.75, Account=Audit Cash, Category=Audit Coffee, Description='Flat white', then went offline and tapped Save. A toast correctly read 'You're offline. We'll retry when you're back.' and the dialog stayed open - but the on-screen Account field snapped back to the default 'Audit Car Loan', Category snapped back to '- Uncategorized -', and Description went blank. Only the Amount field ($4.75) visibly kept its value. This contradicts the form's own documented intent ('a network failure keeps the form filled') in `add-form.tsx`. After going back online and waiting 10s, the transaction DID land correctly with the original Audit Cash / Audit Coffee / 'Flat white' values (confirmed via the account card and the transactions list) - so no data was actually lost - but for as long as the user is offline, the screen actively lies about what it's about to save.
findings.why: A user on a bus with patchy signal is exactly the scenario this feature exists for. Seeing your carefully-chosen account and category vanish the instant you tap Save reads as data loss, and a reasonable response is to re-enter everything (risking a duplicate once the honest queued retry also lands) or to distrust the app's 'we'll retry' promise entirely, even though the underlying retry mechanism is actually working correctly.

findings.issue_key: U00:re authenticate button update mode plaid
findings.element: Re-authenticate button / update-mode Plaid Link flow
findings.experience: Completed the full, correct re-auth: tapped Re-authenticate, went through Plaid's update-mode Link with user_good/pass_good, tapped Finish without saving. Maple showed 'Re-authenticated. Syncing...' - but the pill stayed 'Re-auth needed' the entire time. Two more manual Sync-now taps (both still 'No connected banks to sync.') and two hard reloads later, the item is still 'Re-auth needed', the Recent-syncs log has gained zero new rows since the original failed pull, and /setup still reads 'One bank needs attention.' There is no way, from inside the app, to get this bank syncing again.
findings.why: usePlaidReauth's onSuccess calls `triggerPlaidSync(id)` immediately when Plaid's Link onSuccess fires, and unconditionally sets the notice to 'Re-authenticated. Syncing...' regardless of what that call returns. But the app's own plaid_items.status column is only ever flipped back to 'active' by the ITEM/LOGIN_REPAIRED Plaid webhook handler - nothing in the reauth success path updates it directly. So the immediate triggerPlaidSync call hits the exact same status filter from J14-F2 and silently does nothing, while the UI has already told the user it worked. Nothing else retries it either: the daily cron sweep only ever queries status='active' rows, so a login_required item can never be picked up by the safety net. The user did everything the app asked and is left permanently stuck with no error explaining why.
findings.change: Don't show 'Re-authenticated. Syncing...' until the reauth's own outcome is confirmed - either await a server round-trip that flips status to active (a dedicated endpoint the Link onSuccess calls directly, not a race against a webhook), or have triggerPlaidSync accept login_required items immediately after a successful update-mode Link exchange and clear the status itself instead of relying solely on the webhook. Also have the cron sweep (or a dedicated retry job) periodically re-check login_required items so a webhook that never arrives isn't a permanent dead end.

code_refs.note: onSuccess calls triggerPlaidSync(id) then unconditionally calls onDone -> 'Re-authenticated. Syncing…', without checking the sync result
the ONLY place status is ever set back to 'active' - the LOGIN_REPAIRED webhook handler
safety-net sweep only queries status='active', so it can never pick up or retry a login_required item

findings.issue_key: U19:default sign convention auto respect min
findings.element: Default sign convention ('Auto (respect minus sign)') applied to a pasted CSV
findings.experience: Pasted a 6-row CSV with standard bank-export sign convention (debits negative, e.g. '-184.22' for a Costco purchase; the one credit, an e-transfer, positive '250.00'). The wizard's own live preview showed the correct signs before import ('-$184.22' for Costco, '$250.00' for the e-transfer). After tapping Import, every single row's direction flipped in /transactions: Costco shows '+$184.22' (an inflow), Petro-Canada shows '+$62.40', Amazon shows '+$15.00', and the one genuine inflow, E-TRANSFER RECEIVED, shows '-$250.00' (an outflow).
findings.why: This is the exact scenario the product exists to support - a statement from a bank Plaid can't reach - and it silently corrupts every row's money direction while claiming success ('Imported 6 transactions.'). A household relying on this path to keep their numbers straight now has a wrong outflow/inflow split and, unless they manually check every row against their real statement, a wrong picture of their spending baked into the same uncategorized pile as their bank-synced rows.
findings.change: In wizard.tsx, the field comment on line 84 documents the invariant: 'amountCents: number // signed: positive = outflow'. The 'auto' branch (lines 255-256) currently does `signed = wasNegative ? -Math.abs(amountAbs) : Math.abs(amountAbs)` - a CSV row written as negative (a debit/outflow) ends up with NEGATIVE amountCents, which by the app's own convention means inflow. Flip it to `signed = wasNegative ? Math.abs(amountAbs) : -Math.abs(amountAbs)` (matching the sign the manual-direction branch on line 258 already uses correctly), and add a regression test that pastes a negative-amount CSV row and asserts the resulting transaction renders as an outflow with a minus sign after import, not just that amountCents is negative.

findings.experience: After tapping Add transaction, the button flips to a disabled 'Saving…' and stays there with no toast, no spinner beyond the static label, and no error - observed 48+ seconds and 18+ seconds on two of three submits this session (the third resolved in ~2s). findings.why: A user has no way to distinguish a slow-but-working save from a failed one. findings.issue_key: U20:the whole 5 step auto import setup flow
findings.element: The whole 5-step 'auto-import' setup flow, teased as 'Hands-free' on the parent /transactions/import page

Forward your bank's transaction-alert emails through Gmail... no credentials, no monthly fees.' findings.change: Either relabel the teaser card on /transactions/import - drop 'Hands-free' and 'no credentials, no monthly fees' and replace with something like 'Advanced: Gmail + Apps Script (technical, ~15 min, do this on a computer)' so expectations match reality before anyone taps into it, or add a lightweight 'email me this setup link' action at the very top of the auto-setup page itself so a phone user isn't expected to paste code and juggle multiple tabs on-device.

findings.experience: A non-admin household member opens Setup, sees Rename and Archive controls on every other member's row (not just their own), and can rename or archive another person's household identity with no permission check anywhere - the UI shows the buttons unconditionally and the server action performs the write with no canManageHousehold check.
findings.why: canManage is threaded through MembersList and used correctly to gate InviteForm (line 60) and 'Remove login' (line 340), but the Rename button (line 337) and the Archive ConfirmButton (lines 365-375) render for every viewer regardless of canManage. The underlying server actions renameMember and archiveMember (actions.ts:31,45) only check getHouseholdContext() for household membership, never canManageHousehold - so even a crafted direct form submit from a non-admin succeeds. This is a real authorization gap, not just a display inconsistency: it lets any member alter or hide another member's identity in a finance app, which is exactly the kind of thing that breaks trust.
findings.change: Gate the Rename button and the Archive ConfirmButton behind `canManage` in members-list.tsx (matching the existing Remove-login gate at line 340), AND add a canManageHousehold(ctx) check inside renameMember and archiveMember in actions.ts before the update, returning early (or an error) when the caller lacks permission - client-side gating alone is not sufficient since the action is a server action reachable directly.

findings.experience: The modal's window-level keydown handler treats any Enter press as 'confirm' (confirm-button.tsx:174-176) without checking document.activeElement. findings.element: Add button in the AddCategory form
findings.experience: I tapped Add. The button turned to 'Adding...' after ~1 s, the name field emptied, and then nothing happened - no row under Taxes, no error, no toast - for over six minutes. findings.element: Update balances sheet: balance input + saveBalances
findings.experience: The sheet says 'Enter each account's balance as of August 2026'. The user types today's balance from their statement, taps Save, the sheet shows 'Saved.' and closes, and the ledger shows a different number than they just typed.
findings.why: A snapshot dated YYYY-MM-01 is treated by the engine as the balance at the start of the month; every transaction dated the 2nd through month end is applied on top (balances.ts:86-105, documented in plaid-balances.ts:16-24). The Plaid path rolls the current balance back to the 1st to avoid this (plaid-balances.ts:104-113); the manual path does not, so any account with transactions this month shows typed value minus (or plus) this month's activity. 'The number I typed is not the number shown' destroys trust in the whole sheet.

Alternatively, and simpler for the user: change the copy at form.tsx:56 to 'Enter the balance shown by your bank today' and apply the same rollback. Either way the ledger must display exactly what the user typed for the current month.

A user deleting a wrong 'Tim Hortons -> Groceries' rule expects those rows to go back to uncategorised and finds them still wrong. When sharedCount is 0 the checkbox still offers 'Also unshare the 0 transactions'.

findings.change: Add a second line 'Categories it set stay as they are.' (or a second checkbox 'Also clear the n categories this rule set' that nulls category_id where category_rule_id = id). Hide the unshare checkbox when sharedCount === 0.

findings.element: Sheet option 'Household ratio' (rule-sheet.tsx:237) vs row pill 'Household split' (rules-list.tsx:139); sheet title 'Always do this' (rule-sheet.tsx:115) vs trigger 'Always share' (transactions/row.tsx:302)

findings.element: RecordSettlementForm Field labels; StatTile compact labels; pills
findings.experience: Form labels (FROM, TO, AMOUNT, DATE) are 10px uppercase, stat-tile labels 10px, 'Split 2-way' / 'Rule · name' pills 10px, 'Your share' 10.5px - hard to read on a phone and at larger system font settings they wrap awkwardly.
findings.why: record-form.tsx:135 text-[10px]; stat-tile.tsx:44 text-[10px]; row.tsx:116,120 text-[10px]; page.tsx:397 text-[10.5px].

findings.experience: The chart is titled 'Shared per period' but plots what was owed between members (non-payer shares), not what was spent on shared things; there are no y-axis values and the readouts are hover-only, so on a phone it is a shape with month labels.

findings.change: Rename the label to 'Owed between members, per period' and add the latest value as text beside it ('Last period: $412.10'); or remove the card from this task page and keep it on a report screen.

findings.experience: Every row announces 'Share transaction, toggle button' with no merchant or amount, so a VoiceOver user cannot tell which row they are about to share.
findings.why: row.tsx:78 aria-label is the same string on every row.
findings.change: aria-label={`${isShared ? 'Unshare' : 'Share'} ${t.description ?? 'transaction'}, ${formatMoney(totalAbs)}`}.

findings.experience: A single text-link tap creates a rule and applies it to 12 months of history; the page just refreshes. Payments may appear in past periods with no count of what was recorded and no way back except deleting each.
findings.why: detect-nudge.tsx:21-27 calls createStarterSettlementRule which runs applyRulesToTransactions over 12 months (actions.ts:535-536) and returns no counts.
findings.change: Return {ok, recorded, prompts} from createStarterSettlementRule and toast 'Found 6 e-Transfers - 4 recorded, 2 to confirm'. Or open the existing RuleSheet with the preview count (rule-sheet.tsx:273-283) so the user sees the number before applying.

findings.element: Mark settled, Yes a payment, Record payment, Save split, per-row checkboxes
findings.experience: Up to four leaf-filled primary buttons can be on screen at once across cards, so no single control reads as 'the' action.
findings.why: period-card.tsx:156, payment-prompts.tsx:100, record-form.tsx:113, row.tsx:387 all use variant='primary'.
findings.change: Keep primary for the one action the page is for in its current state (Mark settled when a statement is awaiting, otherwise nothing); demote 'Yes, a payment' to secondary and 'Record payment' to secondary size=md.

findings.experience: The form is the last block on the page; with Amount or Note focused the submit button sits at the bottom edge and is likely under the keyboard, and the Amount field has no enterKeyHint so the keypad offers no 'Done/Go'.
findings.why: record-form.tsx:70-78 (no enterKeyHint), record-form.tsx:113 (submit at the very end); page.tsx:495 places the details last. Severity to be confirmed live (P1 if hidden).
findings.change: Add enterKeyHint='done' to the Amount input and enterKeyHint='send' to Note; move the submit into a sheet-footer when the form is opened from the awaiting card (see U10:record-by-hand-hidden-bottom), or add pb-24 to the details body so the button scrolls above the keyboard.

findings.experience: Amounts only commit on blur; the hidden input posts the last committed cents, so a fast tap on 'Save split' relies on blur beating the submit. If it does not, the previous value is saved silently.
findings.why: money-input.tsx:104-107 commits on blur; row.tsx:364 posts `cents` state, not the raw text. Needs live verification.
findings.change: Post the raw text instead (name on the MoneyInput, parse server-side with parseMoneyToCents) or commit on change with a debounce so the hidden value is always current.

findings.element: PeriodHistory highlightId (?period from /settlements redirect or push)
findings.experience: A push notification about a closed statement lands the user at the top of /shared; the matching period is expanded in 'Past periods' several screens down, but nothing scrolls to it, so the link appears to do nothing.
findings.why: period-history.tsx:32 sets openId from highlightId and gives each <li> an id (line 43) but there is no scrollIntoView / hash. settlements/page.tsx:9 redirects with the query only.
findings.change: In PeriodHistory add useEffect(() => { if (highlightId) document.getElementById(`period-${highlightId}`)?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' }) }, [highlightId]); or redirect to `/shared?period=<id>#period-<id>`.

findings.experience: On a flaky connection or RLS/DB error the user sees 'Nothing recorded for 2026 - Import a statement' even though they have a year of data. They may actually start a manual import.
findings.why: page.tsx:33-50 destructures only `data` from all three queries; `error` is never read. `data` is null on error, `hasAnyActivity` (page.tsx:102) becomes false, and the empty state renders (page.tsx:115-126).
findings.change: Destructure `error` from each query; if any is set, render an error card: title 'Couldn't load this report', body with the plain message, and a `<Link href={currentUrl}>Try again</Link>` Button. Keep the EmptyState strictly for `!error && !hasAnyActivity`.

code_refs.note: empty state shown for null data

findings.experience: At 390px the chart is 440px wide inside ~318px, so months 10-12 are cut off with the scrollbar hidden. In Q4 the selected (current) month is off-screen to the right and the user sees a highlighted column nowhere; nothing hints that the chart pans.
findings.why: page.tsx:171-172 forces `min-w-[440px]` and hides the scrollbar via `.hide-scroll` (globals.css:413-419). Nothing scrolls the selected column into view.
findings.change: Drop `min-w-[440px]` and let 12 columns fit the width (each ~24px bar pair is legible at 140px tall), or keep it and add a right-edge fade (`mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, black 85%, transparent)`) plus a small client effect that calls `el.scrollIntoView({inline:'center'})` on the `[data-selected]` column on mount.

findings.experience: The biggest category's bar is full width but its chip says '34%'; the second bar is 60% of the width but says '20%'. Users read a bar's length as the percentage and the two disagree, which reads as a bug.
findings.why: page.tsx:248 sets width = share of the largest category while page.tsx:249 sets the chip = share of total; role=progressbar at page.tsx:266-270 reports aria-valuenow=sharePct against a visual of widthPct, so screen readers get a third, different reading.
findings.change: Set `widthPct = sharePct` (share of total) so length and label agree, and cap the chip text with 'of spend' only in the aria-label. Replace `role="progressbar"` with `aria-hidden` on the bar and keep the visible name/amount/percent text as the accessible content (a share bar is not a progress indicator).

findings.experience: On the phone the headline numbers read '$3.5K / $2.6K / $890' (rounded to one decimal, so up to $50 vanishes) while on a laptop the same month shows '$3,512.40 / $2,622.10 / +$890.30'. The Net tile also drops its '+' on mobile, so a positive net is only distinguishable by colour and the tiny 'surplus' hint.
findings.why: page.tsx:132-138 pass `compact` to Amount; amount.tsx:29-30 routes compact through formatMoneyCompact which abbreviates at >= $1,000 (format.ts:31-33) and ignores the `sign` prop entirely. The code comment at page.tsx:129 says 'whole dollars' but the output is K-abbreviated.
findings.change: Replace the compact Amount with whole-dollar formatting: add `formatMoneyWhole(cents)` (Intl with maximumFractionDigits:0) and use it in the mobile tiles; for Net pass `sign="always"` and make Amount honour sign in compact mode (amount.tsx:29 branch should prefix '+' when sign==='always' && numeric > 0). Six-digit values still fit three-up at 20px serif ('$12,345').

findings.experience: The one control used on every visit sits at the very top of the page, right under the top bar - the hardest region to reach one-thumb on a 6.1in phone. Flipping back three months means three reaches to the top.
findings.why: page.tsx:110-113 stacks the MonthNav in the header row; on mobile the H1 is sr-only (page-header.tsx:58) so the nav is the first thing at y≈76px. The chart's month links (page.tsx:178) are a mid-page alternative but only for months in view.
findings.change: Move `<MonthNav>` below the tiles (between page.tsx:159 and 163) or render it sticky at the bottom above the tab bar on mobile (`fixed bottom-[calc(var(--tabbar-h)+8px)]`) and keep the top position only from sm: up.

findings.element: Save balances button (form.tsx:67-69) inside the scrolling sheet body
findings.experience: Save sits at the bottom of the scrolling form body, not in the Sheet footer. With 6+ accounts and the keyboard up, the user must dismiss the keyboard and scroll to find it; with the keyboard open on a lower row it is covered.
findings.why: Submit hidden behind the keyboard is a P1 per spec if confirmed live; from code it is at least off-screen on any household with more than about five accounts.
findings.change: Move the Save button and the 'Saved.' live region into the Sheet's footer prop (sheet.tsx:135) so it stays pinned under the scrolling body, and give the form an id so the footer button can use form="balances-form".

findings.element: Update balances sheet Section header Amount (form.tsx:85-93)
findings.experience: The 'Assets' subtotal in the sheet header is a different number from the 'Assets' total on the page behind it for the same month.
findings.why: The sheet sums current_balance_cents ?? opening_balance_cents (raw anchor or opening), the page sums derived balances (page.tsx:116). Two totals with the same label and different values one tap apart.
findings.change: Either pass the derived balance per account into formAccounts and sum that, or remove the subtotal from the sheet header (form.tsx:93) so only one 'Assets' figure exists.

findings.issue_key: list row not a link to detail
findings.experience: A user who sees a wrong balance taps the row and nothing happens. There is no way from here to the account (re-link, fix opening balance, archive) or to the manual entry for just that account.
findings.why: Recognition over recall: the fix lives on /accounts but the page gives no path to it, so the user must remember where balances are managed.
findings.change: Make each row a Link to /accounts#acct-{id} (min-h 44px, full row), with a trailing chevron. For manual accounts, tapping the amount could instead open the Update balances sheet scrolled to that account (pass an initialFocusId to BalanceSheetPanel).

findings.experience: 'Leave a field blank to clear the saved snapshot and fall back to the opening balance.' The household owner does not know what a snapshot or an opening balance is in this app's engine.
findings.why: Internal vocabulary in the one sentence that explains a destructive behaviour.
findings.change: Replace with: 'Type what each account holds today. Credit cards and loans: enter the amount you owe as a positive number.' (and remove the blank-clears rule per U12:blank-clears-snapshot).

findings.element: Liability balance inputs in the sheet (form.tsx:126-134) and Liabilities tile (page.tsx:206-213)
findings.experience: A credit card balance must be typed as a positive amount owed (balances.ts:96-99) but nothing in the sheet says so; a user who types -1200 (as their bank app shows it) makes the liability total negative and net worth jump up. On the page the Liabilities tile shows a positive red number with hint 'Owing', while Net worth may show a red negative number: two red numbers with opposite sign meaning.
findings.why: Sign convention must be stated where the user types and consistent where the user reads.
findings.change: Add a caption under the Liabilities section header in the sheet: 'Enter what you owe as a positive amount.' Reject negative values for liability accounts server-side with a per-field message. On the page keep liabilities unsigned but change the tile hint to 'You owe' and use sign="always" tone="auto" only on Net worth so red = negative applies to one tile only.

findings.element: Balance inputs (form.tsx:126-134): no enterKeyHint, no Enter handling
findings.experience: On iOS the decimal keypad's Return key submits the form after the first field; the sheet shows 'Saved.' and closes while the user still had more accounts to fill.
findings.why: Implicit form submission on a multi-row form; the user has to reopen the sheet and re-find their place.
findings.change: Add enterKeyHint="next" and an onKeyDown that, on Enter, prevents default and focuses the next bal: input (or blurs on the last one). Keep Save as the only submit path.

findings.experience: A sighted user sees a green curve with faint gridlines and a dashed baseline but no month labels and no dollar values on the gridlines; they cannot tell whether the chart spans 6 months or 2 years, or what the swing between its low and high is worth, without scrubbing every point.
findings.why: Only the aria-label (hero.tsx:119) says 'last 24 months'; the gridlines (hero.tsx:135-145) and zero line (hero.tsx:147-155) carry no text. A chart with no period and no scale fails the 'every number answers what is this' trust check and forces recall.
findings.change: Below the <svg> add a 3-label row (flex justify-between, text-[11px] text-ink-3): monthLabel(trail[0].month), monthLabel(trail[12].month), 'Today' - short form e.g. 'Sep 2024'. Add <text> at the right edge of the top and bottom gridlines with fmtCADshort(max) and fmtCADshort(min) from lib/maple.ts:4, and a 'Net worth, last 24 months' caption above the chart when not scrubbing.

findings.experience: The user drags a thumb across the chart to find, say, last Christmas; the label flips to 'December 2025' and the number changes, but the moment they lift the thumb everything snaps back to 'Today'. They cannot read the past value calmly, screenshot it, or compare it to the tiles.
findings.why: hero.tsx:124-125 set scrubIdx to null on pointerup and pointerleave. On a phone there is no hover, so the only way to hold a past month is to keep pressing, which also keeps the finger over the dot and part of the curve. The assets/liabilities tiles (page.tsx:130-147) never follow the scrub either, so the split for that month only lives in the 13.5px delta line.
findings.change: Keep scrubIdx after pointerup (remove the onPointerUp/onPointerLeave resets for pointerType === 'touch'); render a small 'Back to today' ghost button (Button variant ghost, h-11) beside the MapleLabel while a month is pinned, and clear on that tap. Optionally drive the two StatTiles from scrubPoint so the split follows the pinned month.

findings.experience: If Supabase times out or RLS rejects a query, the user is shown 'Nothing to chart yet - Add your accounts and import...' with an 'Add an account' button, as though their linked bank accounts had disappeared. Nothing says it was a failure or offers retry.
findings.why: page.tsx:25-41 destructure only data and never read error; accounts ?? [] at page.tsx:46 and hasData at page.tsx:85 turn any failure into the first-run empty state. For a finance app a wrong 'you have nothing' is a trust break, and the route-level (app)/error.tsx never triggers because nothing throws.
findings.change: Capture error from each query; if any is set, throw new Error('Could not load net worth') so (app)/error.tsx renders, or render <EmptyState title="Couldn't load your net worth" body="Check your connection and pull down to retry." /> with no 'Add an account' CTA. Keep the current empty state only when all three queries succeeded.

findings.experience: The user sees Liabilities $18.2K and wants to know which card or loan that is. The tile does nothing when tapped; the answer is on the balance sheet, which is another More -> Balance sheet trip (2 taps) and a different screen's vocabulary.
findings.why: page.tsx:131-146 render plain StatTiles with no href. Recognition over recall: a total that cannot be expanded forces the user to remember what accounts they have.
findings.change: Wrap each StatTile in <Link href="/balance-sheet"> (or /accounts) with className block and add a foot of 'See accounts ->' (12px) so the tile reads as tappable; keep the 44px min height (compact tile is ~70px). Alternatively list the top 3 accounts per side under the tiles with their balances.

findings.experience: A household with a mortgage sees '−$412,385.20'; at 48px serif inside a card with 24px padding on a 390px screen (about 310px of text width) the figure likely wraps onto two lines or clips, and the tabular digits stop lining up with the label above.
findings.why: hero.tsx:79-85 has no responsive size step, no truncate/min-w-0 and no compact fallback; 12 glyphs at 48px is ~300-330px. Compare stat-tile.tsx:51 which at least truncates. Needs live confirmation of the exact width.
findings.change: Add a size step by length: className text-[40px] when formatted length > 10 characters, text-[48px] otherwise (compute const big = formatted.length > 10), and set overflow-hidden text-ellipsis whitespace-nowrap on the div as a floor. Same fix applies to the dashboard hero.

findings.element: 'Current progress' input defaultValue='0.00' / toFixed(2); 'Target amount' defaultValue in edit
findings.experience: On iOS tapping a prefilled field puts the caret at the end; typing 500 yields '0.00500'. For current progress this parses to null and `?? 0` saves $0.00 with no error; for target it errors 'Target amount must be positive.' which does not describe what went wrong.
findings.why: parseMoneyToCents regex allows at most 2 decimals (format.ts:81) so '0.00500' -> null; actions.ts:25 coalesces null to 0 instead of erroring. Prefill at add-form.tsx:59, row.tsx:196, row.tsx:206.
findings.change: Remove defaultValue='0.00' from add-form.tsx:59 (use placeholder='0.00'). In actions.ts:25 treat an unparsable non-empty current_amount as an error 'Enter progress as dollars and cents, e.g. 1250.00'. In both forms add onFocus={(e) => e.currentTarget.select()} to the amount inputs so an existing value is replaced, not appended.

findings.issue_key: period nav selected period not visible
findings.experience: On the phone the eyebrow and H1 are sr-only because the shell top bar already says 'Contributions'. After tapping '← 2025' the pills read '← 2024 / This year / 2026 →' - the year actually on screen is never shown as a headline; it only appears as 11px hints under two compact tiles. Users lose track of which year they are editing and can save NOA numbers into the wrong year.
findings.why: page-header.tsx:58 applies max-md:sr-only when ShellTitleContext is set; shell.tsx:93 sets it for /contributions; page.tsx:255-277 pills never display the selected year; the only visible year is StatTile hint String(year) at page.tsx:291-292 (11px).
findings.change: Render the selected year as the middle pill ('2026' with aria-current) and move 'This year' to a small reset link that only appears when year !== currentYear; or add a visible 'Room for 2026' heading above the tiles on mobile.

findings.experience: The number the whole screen exists for - room left per account - is a 12px ink-3 caption in the card's top-right, smaller than the 16px input boxes below it. Users read the big inputs as the answer.
findings.why: table.tsx:216-219 renders 'available' + Amount at text-[12px] text-ink-3; the 'Contributed .. of ..' line is 11.5px (table.tsx:237-243) and labels are 10.5px (table.tsx:247).
findings.change: Promote the available amount to font-serif text-[20px] tone leaf/maple as the card's primary number with 'room left' as a 12px label beneath it; keep contributed/of at >=13px.

findings.element: OpeningInput suggested state (border-honey bg-paper-2, placeholder, title tooltip)
findings.experience: That an opening value is 'suggested' is signalled by a honey border colour, a low-contrast placeholder, and a title tooltip that never shows on touch. The sticky-bar sentence 'Honey-bordered inputs are suggested...' asks the user to map a colour name to a field.
findings.why: table.tsx:170-177 (colour + title only); table.tsx:143-146 copy; placeholder colour ink-4 (globals.css:490-493).
findings.change: Add a visible 10.5px 'Suggested' chip beside the label when openingIsSuggestion, render the suggestion as the actual value (see U15:empty-opening-saves-zero), drop the title attribute, and replace the sticky-bar sentence with 'Suggested values are marked' or remove it.

findings.experience: On failure the bar shows 'Could not save your rooms. Please try again.' or 'Your session expired. Please sign in again.' with no link to sign in and no indication which of the 12 fields caused it; the message is 12px and sits above the tab bar, easy to miss after the keyboard closes.
findings.why: actions.ts:23, actions.ts:69 return generic strings; table.tsx:140-141 renders them at text-[12px]; no field association.
findings.change: Render errors at 14px with role=alert, include a 'Sign in' Link for the session case, and (with the field-level errors from U15:malformed-input-silently-zero) scroll the first bad input into view and focus it.

findings.experience: The user opens the native date picker to log a mid-month rate change and, following habit, taps any day (e.g. the 15th) since nothing in the picker itself signals 'first of month only'. Submit fails with 'Effective month must be the first of a month (YYYY-MM-01).'
findings.why: type="date" lets the user select any day; the constraint is enforced only after a round-trip, with an error message that leaks the storage format (YYYY-MM-01) instead of plain language.
findings.change: Change the input to <input type="month" name="effective_month">, which only ever returns a year-month value, then append '-01' server-side before validating/storing. This makes the invalid state unselectable instead of merely rejected. If type="month" support is a concern, at minimum reword the error to 'Pick a month - it always starts on the 1st.' without the ISO token.

findings.experience: With even 2-3 household members, the only Save control sits after every member's card at the very bottom of the page (below the top StatTile grid, below each fieldset); the user must scroll past all entered data to commit it, and there is no persistent way to save mid-scroll.
findings.why: The save bar is plain flow content at the end of the <form>, not sticky (table.tsx:249-263), so it is not in the reachable thumb zone once the household has more than ~1-2 members.
findings.change: Make the save bar `sticky bottom-0` (with safe-area padding) so 'Save hours' stays reachable without scrolling regardless of member count.

code_refs.note: save/status bar is a plain flex row at the end of form flow, not position:sticky

findings.experience: Revoking a pending invitation happens on a single tap with no confirm step, sitting in the same compact action row where every other consequential action on this screen (Archive member, Remove login) opens a confirm sheet with a description of the consequence first.
findings.why: revokeInvitation is called directly from the button's onClick-wrapped form submit (members-list.tsx:247) with no ConfirmButton wrapper, breaking the pattern established at lines 341 and 365 for equally-reversible-but-consequential actions.
findings.change: Wrap the Revoke action in the same ConfirmButton component used for Archive/Remove-login, with prompt e.g. "Revoke invite to {invite.email}?" and description "They won't be able to use that invite link anymore. You can invite them again anytime."

code_refs.note: revokeInvitation fired with no confirm modal

findings.experience: A user can check/uncheck several notification toggles (e.g. turn on 'Every new transaction', turn off 'Large transactions only') and, unlike the split-weights form which disables Save until something actually changed and clearly signals 'dirty', this form's Save button is always enabled and gives no warning if the user navigates away before tapping it - the toggles just silently revert to whatever was last saved.
findings.why: saveNotificationPrefs (notification-actions.ts) is only invoked on explicit form submit; the <form> at notifications.tsx:177 has no dirty-state tracking or beforeunload/navigation guard, unlike split-weights-form.tsx which computes `dirty` (line 21) and disables Save until something changed - so there is no visual cue here that unsaved changes exist at all.
findings.change: Track dirty state on the notification-prefs form the same way split-weights-form.tsx does, and show an 'unsaved changes' inline warning (or auto-save on toggle, which would also remove the separate Save button) so a toggle flip is never silently lost.

findings.element: CSV column mapping -> Category field, csvPreviewRows category resolution
findings.experience: A row whose CSV 'Category' text doesn't match any existing category name/code silently becomes Uncategorized with no indication the mapped value failed to resolve, distinguishing it from a row that genuinely had no category.
findings.why: A user who mapped a Category column expecting it to work sees the same 'Uncategorized' label as a row that never had a category at all, so they can't tell their mapping is broken versus the source data being blank.
findings.change: In csvPreviewRows (wizard.tsx:225-228), when the mapped Category text is non-empty but neither categoryByCode nor categoryByName resolves it, keep the raw text and render it as e.g. 'Unmatched: "<value>"' instead of collapsing straight to 'Uncategorized' (derivePreview, wizard.tsx:720).

code_refs.note: category lookup falls back silently to null
unmatched category renders identically to a blank category

findings.experience: The commit button sits in normal document flow after the paste/upload step, the mapping grid, and a preview list/table that can itself scroll internally up to 420px tall - on a real statement with many rows the primary action can end up well below the fold.
findings.why: Violates the bottom-third/one-thumb reachability rule for the primary CTA: a household owner with 5-15 seconds of attention has to scroll past a variable-height preview before they can even see the button that finishes the job.
findings.change: Make the commit <form> (wizard.tsx:690-704) a sticky-bottom bar (`sticky bottom-0` with safe-area padding, matching the rest of the app's bottom-bar convention) once readyCount > 0, so the Import button stays reachable regardless of preview length.

findings.issue_key: content dev instructions in prod ui
findings.experience: When SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is unset, the page renders instructions to add it to .env.local and 'restart the dev server' directly in the product UI.
findings.why: An end user in production cannot edit a local .env file or restart a dev server; this message can only be actioned by a developer, so any real user who hits it (e.g. a misconfigured prod deploy) is stuck with unusable instructions and no path forward.
findings.change: Detect environment (dev vs prod) and, in production, replace the .env.local/restart wording with 'This household's auto-import isn't fully configured yet - contact support' (or hide the whole banner in prod and rely on server-side monitoring/alerting instead), keeping the current developer-facing copy only for local/dev builds.

code_refs.note: hasServiceRoleKey banner with .env.local / restart dev server instructions, rendered unconditionally on env

findings.element: Copy buttons for Webhook URL, secret, and Code.gs script
findings.experience: `navigator.clipboard?.writeText(value).then(() => setCopied(...))` has no `.catch()`. If the clipboard write is rejected (denied permission, non-secure context, older mobile browser), nothing happens: no error, no 'Copied' confirmation, no fallback selection of the text.
findings.why: A user who taps Copy, sees no feedback, and pastes into the Gmail script or a note gets nothing - and has no way to know the copy silently failed versus succeeded, on the one field (the secret) they only get to see once.

findings.element: 'Save terms' button on the loan-terms form (loans/form.tsx submit)
findings.experience: After tapping Save terms, the button flips to a disabled 'Saving…' and stays there for 38+ seconds of active watching, with no spinner, no toast, no progress indicator. The underlying POST /loans request actually completed with a 200 well within the first few seconds (confirmed in the network log), but the client-side UI never reflects it - only a full page reload reveals the terms saved correctly.
findings.why: This is the same class of hung-save bug documented repeatedly in earlier journeys (category adds, budget edits, transaction adds, rules) - a revalidatePath fan-out or client transition that doesn't settle even though the server-side mutation succeeded almost instantly. On a phone, a user has no way to distinguish this from a genuinely broken save and will very plausibly re-tap, navigate away thinking it failed, or wait far longer than necessary.
findings.change: Resolve the pending/Saving… client state directly from the server action's own return value/promise resolution rather than relying on Next's revalidation+re-render cycle to settle it - the fix should make the button return to its resting state within roughly 1-2 seconds of the actual server response, matching what the 'Add' rate-change control on this same page already does correctly.

findings.why: The brief expected 'browser will likely deny' the permission prompt, but on this platform there is no prompt to deny at all - the feature is invisible outside an installed iOS Safari PWA, even though Chrome/Edge/Firefox all support the exact same Push API this code already calls. A user who reads 'notify me the moment a transaction lands' and checks every box below it has no way to know none of it can ever fire without a completely separate, unmentioned installation ritual.
findings.change: In notifications.tsx, split the standalone check: keep the iOS-specific 'Add to Home Screen' messaging only for iOS Safari (detect via userAgent/navigator.standalone), and show the real 'Enable notifications' button directly in any other Push-API-supporting browser (window.matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches should not gate Chrome/Edge/Firefox, which support Web Push in a normal tab).

findings.experience: If navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js') rejects (blocked by browser policy, storage quota, private mode, etc.), the only trace is a console.warn - the user sees no difference and never learns why install, offline fallback, and push notifications aren't working for them.

screens: /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html (+ install hint / update toast overlays rendered on every app route)
findings.experience: The branded offline.html only ever shows on a hard/full page navigation. If a user loses connectivity while already inside the installed app and taps a normal in-app link (client-side App Router navigation, which fetches the RSC payload), that fetch is deliberately excluded from SW handling and just fails - the user gets whatever Next's default client-side fetch-error behavior is, not the reassuring 'You're offline / Try again' screen.
findings.why: isNextRouterRequest() (sw.js:165-175) returns true for RSC/prefetch requests and the fetch handler returns early for them (sw.js:129-131) before any caching logic runs; only req.mode === 'navigate' gets networkFirstPage's offline.html fallback (sw.js:149-154). Losing network mid-session - the common real-world case for a phone walking out of coverage - is the one case the fallback doesn't cover.
findings.change: In sw-registrar.tsx or a lightweight app-shell listener, catch Next's client-router navigation failures (or listen for `online`/`offline` events) and surface the same offline messaging/card in-app (not a full navigation to offline.html) when a client-side route fetch fails, so the experience is consistent regardless of how connectivity was lost.

findings.element: App-wide typography (labels, amounts, hints, section headers)
findings.experience: Virtually every text size in the reviewed files is a hardcoded Tailwind arbitrary px value rather than a rem-based scale: MapleLabel is 11px (label.tsx:16), Field's label is 10.5px (field.tsx:32), dashboard section labels are 10-11.5px (dashboard/client.tsx:217, 280, 497, 530), globals.css pins inputs at a literal 16px (globals.css:191, 469, 531). None of this is tied to the root font size.
findings.why: The unit's 'largest system font size' check fails app-wide: a low-vision user who increases their OS/browser text-size preference gets no change to any label, amount, or hint in Maple - the smallest labels (10.5-11px) stay illegibly small regardless of the accessibility setting they've turned on.
findings.change: Move the type scale to rem units (e.g. define a `--font-size-*` scale in rem in globals.css and swap the arbitrary px classes for it), keeping the one hard 16px-minimum rule for iOS input zoom-prevention as the sole documented px exception.

findings.experience: The mapping dropdown offers a 'Direction' field (wizard.tsx:25) whose auto-detected values are parsed from raw bank vocabulary like DR/CR, debit/credit (wizard.tsx:234-241), with no plain-language example shown to the user choosing this mapping.
findings.why: A household owner who isn't familiar with statement terminology may not recognize what 'Direction' means or which of their columns qualifies, undermining H2 (match to user vocabulary).
findings.change: Relabel the option to something like 'Direction (in/out, debit/credit)' in FIELD_OPTIONS (wizard.tsx:18-26), or add a one-line example under the Step 2 header the first time a Direction column is detected.

findings.element: match_from, match_subject, description_regex, date_regex, inflow_regex inputs on the rule form
findings.experience: readRuleFromForm only runs `new RegExp()` validation on amount_regex and account_router_regex; the other five regex-shaped fields are trimmed and stored as-is with no syntax check.
findings.why: A typo'd bracket in, say, the subject regex saves successfully and only surfaces later as an opaque ingestion failure far from where the mistake was made, instead of being caught at submit time next to the field.
findings.change: Wrap every regex-shaped field in the same try/new RegExp()/catch validation used for amount_regex, returning the same field-specific error message pattern.
