findings.element: Setup progress bar / 'X / Y done' summary
findings.experience: The progress summary tallies only steps 1, 3, 4, 5 (`trackable = [1, 3, 4, 5]`) against a denominator of 4, while 5 numbered steps are visibly rendered on the page; step 2 always shows a neutral 'At your bank' pill that never turns into 'Done'.
findings.why: A user counting the 5 visible steps against a '3/4' or '4/4 - ready' summary can reasonably conclude a step is missing or broken, undermining the one piece of at-a-glance status this wizard provides (H1).
findings.change: Either count all 5 steps with step 2 defaulting to an explicit self-check ('I've turned this on' toggle the user can tick), or relabel the summary to 'X of 4 automatic steps' so the excluded manual step is explained inline rather than silently absent from the math.

findings.experience: 'Used once at sign-in. We never see it.' sits under the password field (sign-up/page.tsx:74-76). Taken literally this says the password is used only the first time, which is false - it's used on every sign-in.
findings.why: H2 - copy should match the user's mental model in plain language; this phrasing is ambiguous enough to read as a factual claim about the product that isn't true, which is a trust risk in a finance app.
findings.change: Reword to something unambiguous, e.g. 'Stored securely - we never see it in plain text.'

findings.experience: resend-button.tsx:19 disables the button once `sent` is true and there is no path back to enabled without a full page reload, even after Supabase's own one-per-minute rate limit window has passed.
findings.why: H3/H7 - a real user waiting on a missing email who wants to try again after 60s has no in-page way to do so.
findings.change: After a successful send, start a 60s countdown (matching Supabase's own rate limit) and re-enable the button with label 'Resend confirmation email' when it elapses, instead of disabling permanently for the component's lifetime.

findings.element: Email input on sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password
findings.experience: None of the first-field inputs (sign-in/page.tsx:42, sign-up/page.tsx:53, forgot-password/page.tsx:62) set autoFocus, so on desktop/keyboard entry the user must tap the field before typing; on mobile this is minor since tapping the field is the norm anyway.
findings.why: H7 (efficiency) - a one-tap-fewer opportunity for the most common screens in the app.
findings.change: Add autoFocus to the email input on sign-in and sign-up (skip on mobile-only screens if it fights the mobile keyboard-open animation; verify live).

findings.element: Household name + display name inputs, src/app/onboarding/form.tsx:41-68
findings.experience: Step 1 asks for two free-text names (household name, display name) before the user has connected anything or seen any value. This is the product's minimum viable input (2 fields) and is skippable only in the sense that nothing downstream needs it, but there's no 'skip' on this particular step - it's the mandatory gate.
findings.why: Matches the spec's '<=3 inputs before value' bar so this is not a violation, but it's worth flagging that unlike every later step this one has no Skip/Back option at all (correctly, since a household must exist) - callers should confirm this is intentional and not an oversight.
findings.change: No change required; documented for completeness. If product wants literal zero required inputs, a default household name (e.g. "My household") could be pre-filled so only the display name blocks progress.

findings.issue_key: action throws instead of returning error
findings.experience: completeOnboarding calls RPC complete_onboarding with no explicit error surfaced to the UI beyond `throw new Error(error.message)`; StepFooter's onClick wraps this in useTransition with no catch (step-footer.tsx:42), so a thrown error becomes an unhandled promise rejection / React error boundary trip rather than a message next to the Skip button.
findings.why: If the RPC ever fails (e.g. network hiccup, permission edge case for a non-owner who somehow reaches a skip='finish' step), the user sees a broken page/blank error boundary instead of an inline message telling them what happened and what to do - violates error recovery next to the control.
findings.change: Have completeOnboarding return a result object ({ok:true}|{error}) like the other actions, and show the error inline near the Skip button in StepFooter instead of throwing.

findings.experience: Multiple pending invites can be listed for one email (invites.map). Clicking Join on one submits acceptInvitationById and on success does router.replace('/onboarding/welcome') (line 34), but the other invites for the same email are never invalidated in the UI - a user could tap Join on a second invite row before navigation completes.
findings.why: Low probability edge case (double invite for same email) but there's no client-side guard disabling sibling rows once one Join is in flight, only the clicked button's own `pending` state (shared useTransition, so actually all buttons share one `pending` flag from `useTransition()` at line 12 - re-check: pending is a single shared boolean, so this is actually fine, all Join buttons disable together).
findings.change: No change needed - the shared `pending` from the single useTransition already disables every Join button while one is in flight.

findings.experience: Budget inputs are plain text with inputMode=decimal but no placeholder pattern guidance beyond '0', no maxLength, and no client-side parsing/formatting (no cents conversion shown, no $-prefixed live formatting as typed) - a user could type '12.5', '1250', or '1,250.00' and not know which convention the app expects until they see the save result (or an error) on the next screen/page.
findings.why: Finance-check '12.50 vs 1250 handling' from the spec is unverifiable from this file alone since the actual parsing lives in saveBudgets (not in the files list for this unit) - flagging for the live check, since a wrong-order-of-magnitude budget silently saved would badly undermine trust (a hidden P1 if parsing is naive).
findings.change: Confirm saveBudgets (src/app/(app)/budgets/actions.ts) parses these dollar strings correctly and rejects/normalizes ambiguous input; add inline formatting (mask to 2 decimals) so the user sees their number is understood as dollars before submitting.

findings.experience: Back and Skip are rendered in a left-aligned row (sm:flex-row-reverse puts Continue on the right on desktop, but on mobile flex-col stacks Continue on top, Back+Skip below it) - Back sits in the footer row below the card, which is good (bottom-third), but it's a small 44px-min-height text link, not a distinct affordance separate from Skip, and both share one row with tiny gap-1 spacing (line 70).
findings.why: Back and Skip are visually similar (same font size/weight, adjacent, gap-1 ~4px) risking a mis-tap between 'go back' and 'abandon this step and finish onboarding' - a mis-tap on Skip when meaning Back is a meaningfully different, harder-to-undo outcome (ends the guided flow / lands on dashboard) sitting right next to a low-stakes action.
findings.change: Add clearer visual separation (larger gap, a vertical divider, or move Skip to its own row) between Back and Skip so a thumb can't easily hit the wrong one, especially since Skip('finish') has larger consequence than Back.

findings.experience: Pending invites show 'Invite sent' and joined members show 'Joined' as the only status text (lines 76, 82) - no indication of when it was sent, whether it's close to the 7-day expiry mentioned in the footnote, or a way to resend/revoke from this screen.
findings.why: If an invite silently expires and the owner doesn't come back to /setup, the invitee link breaks with no visible warning during onboarding itself - a minor trust gap since the footnote claims 7-day expiry but the list gives no per-invite timing info.
findings.change: Show relative expiry ('expires in 5 days') per pending invite, or at least link 'Manage invites' to Setup from this screen.

findings.issue_key: U13:trend chart line sept 2024 may 2026 segm
findings.element: trend chart line, Sept 2024 - May 2026 segment
findings.experience: 20 of the chart's 24 monthly data points (Sept 2024 through May 2026) show the exact same net worth, $100,645.78, to the penny - a dead-flat line spanning over 80% of the chart's width - before a real, dramatic 3-month story (June-Aug 2026) plays out in the final sliver. This flat stretch is the accounts' opening-balance backfill, not real financial history, but it is drawn with the identical solid green stroke as the real portion.
findings.why: The only hint this isn't real is 'Building a year of history…', a small gray caption below the headline number, disconnected from the graphic. A user skimming the chart's shape - especially paired with the page's own heading 'Two years of patience.' - could easily read 20 flat months as genuine stability rather than a backfill artifact.
findings.change: Visually distinguish the backfilled segment before earliestRealMonth (already computed server-side) - e.g. a dashed or lighter stroke, or simply clip the chart to only the months with real data until enough history accumulates.

findings.element: "Paid by" select in the rule form
findings.experience: The default-payer dropdown only ever offers 'Account owner (or joint)' and, if the signed-in user has a member id, 'Me' - there is no option to default a rule to any other household member.
findings.why: The product model centers on splitting shared expenses across 1..N household members; a rule that always defaults incoming card alerts to only the signer or 'joint' can't represent a household where a specific other member's card is the one emailing alerts, forcing manual correction on every imported transaction from that card.
findings.change: Populate the select from all active household members (not just the current session's member id), the same way categories/accounts are already listed.

findings.element: OpenPeriodCard 'Open since …' vs MonthNav calendar month
findings.experience: The running tally says 'Open since Sep 28 · closes Oct 28' while the flag list is scoped to 'October 2026' with a month nav. A user who flags a Sep 29 grocery row must switch the month nav back to September even though it belongs to the open period shown above.
findings.why: page.tsx:64 scopes the list by calendar month while settlement periods are close-day based (settlement.ts:290-312).
findings.change: Scope the flag list by the open period by default (period_start..today) and label the nav 'This period' with ‹ › stepping through closed periods; keep ?month only as a deep link. At minimum, add the period dates to the transactions card header: 'Transactions on Visa · Sep 28 - today'.

findings.element: Move up / Move down 44x44 buttons, gap-0.5 (rules-list.tsx:163-178); reorderRule rewrites every rule row (actions.ts:234)
findings.experience: Each arrow tap is a server action that rewrites sort_order for all rules and refreshes the page; the card jumps only after the round-trip, and both arrows disable while pending. The two opposite-direction arrows are 2px apart. Moving a rule from bottom to top of 8 rules is 7 round-trips.
findings.why: Ordering matters ('first match decides') but is slow and fiddly.
findings.change: Swap only the two affected rows in reorderRule and apply the reorder optimistically in RulesList state; increase the vertical gap to gap-2. Consider a long-press drag handle for lists > 4.

findings.experience: On the dashboard the user can tap the eye to blur balances before showing the phone to someone; on Net worth, the single largest number in the app, there is no such control and the dashboard's choice does not carry over.
findings.why: dashboard/client.tsx:147, 237-241, 284 keep hidden as local component state and wrap figures in PrivacyBlur; hero.tsx:78-85 and page.tsx:131-146 render raw. Hide-sensitive should be one tap anywhere and consistent.
findings.change: Move hidden into a small context in the shell (persist in localStorage key maple.hideBalances), expose the eye toggle in the mobile top bar next to Settings for every route, and wrap the hero figure, delta line and both tile values in PrivacyBlur.

findings.experience: A household past 20,000 transactions would silently get a wrong net worth (older rows dropped, balances shifted) with no warning.
findings.why: page.tsx:36-40 fetch every transaction with no date floor and a hard limit; with Plaid pulling two years of history for several accounts this is reachable, and snapshots only anchor accounts that have them.
findings.change: Either compute balances server-side (a SQL view per account-month) or fetch only rows with occurred_on >= the earliest month needed after the newest snapshot; if the limit is still hit, log and render a small 'History truncated' notice instead of a silently wrong number.

findings.experience: After confirming removal of a rate change there is no undo; if the household member picks the wrong row despite the confirm sheet, the only recovery is re-typing the deleted rate change from memory.
findings.why: Product model favours undoable/logged edits; deleteRateChange performs a hard delete with no soft-delete/undo affordance, unlike other destructive flows in the app that pair confirm with a follow-up undo toast.
findings.change: Add a brief 'Rate change removed. Undo' toast after deleteRateChange succeeds, backed by re-inserting the same row (id, effective_month, annual_rate_bps, note) if Undo is tapped within a few seconds.

findings.element: Field labels and hint text across every card on this screen
findings.experience: Nearly every label and hint on the page - close-day helper, member role hint, invite email hint, split-weight percent text, notification threshold label, toggle hints - renders between 10.5px and 13px, well under the 16px body-text legibility bar.
findings.why: Representative instances: close-day helper 'text-[11px]' (close-day-form.tsx:37), member sub-text 'text-[11.5px]' (members-list.tsx:239), split-weight percent 'text-[12px]' (split-weights-form.tsx:52), notification threshold label 'text-[12.5px]' (notifications.tsx:171), toggle hint 'text-[11.5px]' (notifications.tsx: Toggle component hint span).
findings.change: Raise recurring hint/helper text to at least 13-14px minimum (16px for anything a user must read to act, not just decorative captions) across the shared Field/label components so the fix propagates everywhere this pattern is used, not just on this screen.

findings.element: RuleForm field grid (11 fields + template select + Smart Suggester)
findings.experience: The open rule form presents name, enabled, from-regex, subject-regex, amount-regex, description-regex, date-regex, sign convention, inflow-regex (conditional), account-router-regex, fallback account, paid-by, and default category - 11+ inputs in one uninterrupted section.
findings.why: Exceeds Hick's-law guidance of >5 choices in one group and, on a 390px-wide viewport with two-column fields collapsing to one column, produces a long uninterrupted scroll that makes it easy to lose track of which fields are required vs optional.
findings.change: Group the form into two disclosures - 'Required to save' (name, amount regex, fallback account) always visible, and 'Matching details' (the remaining regex/router/default fields) collapsed by default with a summary of how many are filled in, similar to how Smart Suggester is already collapsed.
